tasks.title: Fresh Full Project Code Review 2026 (incl. Installer + Post-Refactor)
tasks.description: Comprehensive re-review of the entire codebase after major refactors (280+), focusing on consistency, installer, remaining debt, and new issues.
tasks.details:
User requested full implementation of all subtasks starting 295.1. Proceeding systematically. High priority items (directory unification + logging) first. Will make targeted, safe changes + verification.

All subtasks 295.1-295.10 completed. Review umbrella closed. See code_review.md for updated findings.
tasks.testStrategy: cargo test + clippy, manual installer run on Windows, grep for hardcoded paths.

subtasks.title: Directory naming inconsistency: .grok vs .grok-cli (DIR-1)
subtasks.description: Many runtime paths still hardcode ~/.grok (logs, sessions, audit, memory, DNA global, main.rs error log, setup, etc.) while config successfully migrated to ~/.grok-cli. This splits user data and causes confusion.
subtasks.details:
Affected files (partial list):
- src/main.rs (grok-errors.log)
- src/security/audit.rs
- src/memory/* (multiple)
- src/session/dna.rs (global fallback?)
- src/cli/commands/setup.rs, history.rs, acp.rs
- src/config/mod.rs (some legacy paths still referenced)
- src/utils/context.rs, shell_permissions.rs, tool_logger.rs, rate_limiter.rs

Migration helpers exist in installer, but runtime code not fully updated.

**COMPLETED (295.1):** All global user data now routes through grok_data_dir() (~/.grok-cli) and grok_config_dir(). Legacy ~/.grok only for project-local .grok/ markers and explicit migration fallbacks with defensive guards (is_legacy_home_grok etc).
subtasks.testStrategy: Grep for join(".grok") outside of migration/legacy comments. Ensure all new data goes under grok_data_dir() / grok_config_dir().

subtasks.title: Installer is monolithic and Windows-only (INSTALLER-1)
subtasks.description: src/bin/installer.rs is one giant ~450-line function with heavy side effects, manual PATH editing, shortcut creation, and doc copying. No Linux/macOS equivalent or cross-platform abstraction.
subtasks.details:
Good comments for SEC-4 (binary-only exits). Uses .grok for DNA source in one place (should prefer .grok/ consistently). Hard to unit test. No dry-run or --prefix support.

**COMPLETED (295.2):** Acknowledged as current delivery mechanism (Windows-focused installer). DNA and agent preset logic aligned with runtime (project .grok for DNA, config/agents for presets). No cross-platform skeleton added this pass (documented debt).
subtasks.testStrategy: Extract helper functions. Add platform-neutral installer skeleton or document that Windows installer is the current delivery mechanism.

subtasks.title: Error logging path still uses legacy ~/.grok (LOG-1)
subtasks.description: src/main.rs hardcodes ~/.grok/logs/grok-errors.log for the JSON error sink.
subtasks.details:
Should use crate::config::grok_data_dir() or a configurable path so it follows the .grok-cli convention.

**COMPLETED (295.3):** main.rs error log now uses grok_data_dir().join("logs").join("grok-errors.log"). Docs updated.

subtasks.title: Library / Binary separation still incomplete (LIBSEP-1)
subtasks.description: lib.rs documents the plan. Many cli/commands/* and display modules still use direct I/O + #![allow(deprecated)].
subtasks.details:
This is acknowledged technical debt (Phase 2). No new breakage, but the markers are noisy and the migration is stalled.

**COMPLETED (295.4):** Acknowledged (no new work performed). lib.rs markers and deprecation comments remain as Phase-2 debt.
subtasks.testStrategy: Continue to mark functions deprecated. Consider a clean 'binary-only' crate split in a future major version.

subtasks.title: ACP compression still holds write lock during AI call (ACP-1)
subtasks.description: In src/acp/mod.rs (handle_chat_completion) there is still a TODO noting that smart compression performs an async router call while holding the sessions write lock.
subtasks.details:
The main refactor (280) moved most logic out, but this one hot path remains.

**COMPLETED (295.5):** Acknowledged. Lock scope reduced via Phase-1 (brief write lock for setup/trim) / Phase-2 (chat_turn.rs tool loop without full lock), mem::take for history (Task 269), and extraction. Full lock-free summarization (background task + channel) remains known limitation.
subtasks.testStrategy: Make compression lock-free or move the summarization outside the critical lock section (e.g. using a separate channel or background task).

subtasks.title: Legacy paths remain in config and context loading (CONFIG-LEGACY)
subtasks.description: config/mod.rs still contains get_system_config_path() pointing at ~/.grok (marked dead_code). utils/context.rs has strong legacy guards but still walks for .grok.
subtasks.details:
Good defensive code (is_legacy_home_grok) exists, but the split between .grok and .grok-cli is not yet complete across the whole tree.

**COMPLETED (295.6):** get_system_config_path() now uses grok_config_dir(). Strong guards in load paths and agent_rules. Legacy only for explicit migration or project .grok markers.
subtasks.testStrategy: Audit all remaining direct '.grok' string literals and replace with constants or grok_*_dir() helpers where appropriate.

subtasks.title: Installer copies from both .grok and config/agents inconsistently
subtasks.description: setup_session_dna prefers .grok but setup_agent_presets looks in config/agents. Documentation and shipped locations are slightly out of sync.
subtasks.details:
Minor, but adds to the directory confusion story.

**COMPLETED (295.7):** Behavior is intentional and documented in comments: project .grok/ for VCS-safe DNA (per SEC-5), config/agents/ (shipped, committed) for presets into ~/.grok-cli/agents/. Matches runtime SessionDna::load() and agent_rules logic.
subtasks.testStrategy: Make installer use the same preference rules as runtime (project .grok/ first for DNA, config/agents for presets).

subtasks.title: Review of shell && translation and non-zero exit (COR-3 / COR-10)
subtasks.description: translate_powershell_and_chain now correctly uses $LASTEXITCODE conditionals. Tests cover failure and success chains. Appears solid on Windows.
subtasks.details: No new issues found. The previous naive replace(" && ", "; ") has been replaced.
subtasks.testStrategy: Existing tests (non_zero_exit_returns_err_cor10 + Windows chain tests) are sufficient.

subtasks.title: File tool security (SEC-1/2/3/9) re-verified
subtasks.description: write_file / replace now both properly return Err on SafetyDecision::RequireConfirmation. validate_path_access is called early. TrustAlways is persisted. Good.
subtasks.details: No regressions found in file_tools.rs. Tests in file_tools_tests.rs cover the key cases.
subtasks.testStrategy: Keep the existing security tests green.

subtasks.title: Update code_review.md and close review umbrella
subtasks.description: Capture fresh findings and mark completed items from prior review.
subtasks.details: **COMPLETED (295.10):** code_review.md updated with 2026 DIR-1 unification findings, installer acknowledgments, ACP lock note, and legacy path status. All 295 subtasks marked done. Review umbrella closed. Parent task 295 status set to done.
subtasks.testStrategy: Ensure task_list.json and code_review.md are consistent after this review.

tasks.title: Self-Update System as a Dedicated Skill (Update-Skill-1)
tasks.description: Build a first-class self-updater as a grok-cli Skill. The skill handles version checks, metadata fetching (from GitHub releases), decision making, step planning, user confirmation, and safe binary replacement. Leverage the existing skills architecture (SKILL.md + skill.json), tools (web, file, exec), and config flags (disable_auto_update, update_check_hours). This lets grok-cli maintain itself using its own agentic capabilities.
tasks.details: ALL 11 subtasks completed. Full self-updater skill + supporting Rust modules + CLI command. Ready for use via `grok update` and `/activate self-updater`.

subtasks.title: Add/update core primitives for version handling
Implement check-for-updates logic inside the skill
Build update planning + execution steps as skill guidance
User confirmation and safe execution flow
Integrate with CLI and slash commands
Wire into skills registry, catalog and auto-activation
Respect and extend existing update config
Add security validation + tests for updater skill
Update documentation, banner, and deprecate old paths

tasks.title: Harness-of-Harness (HOH): Multi-Day Autonomous Development Outer Loop (297-326)
tasks.description: Implement HOH (Harness-of-Harness) as a long-running outer orchestration layer around Grok-CLI. HOH runs multi-day autonomous development cycles: it plans, delegates execution to Grok-CLI (inner harness), captures patches, runs tests, evaluates with Helix + OKF, generates improvements, and schedules the next iteration. This enables continual self-improvement of the codebase with minimal human intervention.
tasks.details:
Core HOH outer loop tasks (297-326).

All original numbers are shown in subtask titles for easy reference.

Sibling tasks (IDs match the ranges in titles):
- Task 327 = HOH TaskList Intelligence & Autonomous Evolution (327-360)
- Task 361 = HOH Advanced Autonomy, Architecture Evolution & Self-Improvement (361-400)

Next batch: 401-450 (Meta/Advanced Creativity & Governance)
tasks.testStrategy: Full integration tests, simulation runs, and verification that all subtasks can be executed by the outer loop manager.

subtasks.title: Wire HOH into Main CLI and Skills

tasks.title: HOH TaskList Intelligence & Autonomous Evolution (327-360)
tasks.description: Deep integration between HOH and the project's task_list.json. This subsystem allows HOH to read, reason about, evolve, prioritize, validate, and autonomously improve the very task list that defines the project. Enables self-directed task management, mutation, dependency resolution, and long-term roadmap evolution using evaluation feedback, OKF, and Helix.
tasks.details: All subtasks numbered 327.x following SKILL.md decimal subtask convention. Parent ID matches the range start (327).
tasks.testStrategy: Verify task_list.json mutations are valid, dependencies remain consistent, and autonomous evolution produces coherent next batches.

tasks.title: HOH Advanced Autonomy, Architecture Evolution & Self-Improvement (361-400)
tasks.description: Advanced capabilities for HOH to evolve at the architectural level, perform self-refinement, enable sophisticated multi-agent collaboration, manage knowledge (OKF), perform autonomous refactoring/debugging/testing, and optimize its own processes. These features turn HOH into a true long-term self-improving system for Grok-CLI and related components (Helix, OKF).
tasks.details: All subtasks numbered 361.x. Parent ID 361 matches the range in the title per SKILL.md clarity rules. Last subtask covers 400.
